# Balls from ASSS 1.4.4 src/core/balls.c (compiled unmodified).
#   # <label>   starts a scenario; 'settings' is what load_ball_settings read
#      from [Soccer] at AA_CREATE, with the four spawn points as x,y,radius
#   uniforms <n> <v>...  the PRNG draws queued for the step that follows; they are
#      consumed in order, two per ball placement
#   solid <n> <x,y>...   the tiles FindEmptyTileNear must move a ball off
#   seat <triples>   one per player: freq digit, 'w' in a ship or 's' spec, then
#      '.' normal or 'l' flagged too lagged to carry (flags.no_flags_balls)
#   spawn <ball>     called SpawnBall directly
#   pickup <player> <ball> time=<n> len=<n>   fed a C2S 0x20 of that length
#   fire <player> <ball> <x> <y> <xspeed> <yspeed> time=<n>   fed a C2S 0x1F
#   goal <player> <ball> <x> <y>   fed a C2S 0x21
#   kill <killer> <killed>   ran the kill handler
#   leave <player>   ran the PA_LEAVEARENA action
#   pkt <hex>        each S2C 0x2E ball packet, in order and in wire order
#   cb <name>        each callback fired, in order
#   balls <n> <bid>:<state>/<x>/<y>/<xspeed>/<yspeed>/<carrier>/<time>...
#      every ball afterwards; carrier -1 means nobody
#
# Rules these records pin:
#
# 1. WHICH SPAWN POINT A BALL USES is decided by how many are CONFIGURED, and the
#    test is 'spawnx[3] && spawny[3]' then 'spawnx[1] && spawny[1]' -- both
#    coordinates must be NON-ZERO. So a legitimate spawn point on row 0 or column
#    0 silently drops the arena to fewer spawn points: setting SpawnX3 to 0
#    because you want x=0 turns a four-point arena into a two-point one.
#    With four configured the index is bid % 4, with two it is bid % 2.
# 2. THE SPAWN OFFSET IS TRUNCATED, NOT ROUNDED, and the truncation is applied to
#    the OFFSET, not to the final coordinate: x = cx + (int)(rndrad * cos(rndang)).
#    Compare fg_wz.py, which adds half a tile to the centre and truncates the sum
#    -- the two flag/ball spawners in the same server round differently.
# 3. THE WRAP IS A MODULO, NOT A REFLECTION: 'while (x < 0) x += 1024' and
#    'while (x > 1023) x -= 1024'. fg_wz.py's wrap() for flags reflects instead.
#    A ball drawn off the left edge comes back on the right; a flag bounces.
# 4. THE SUB-TILE POSITION COMES FROM ONE 32-BIT DRAW. After the tile is chosen the
#    coordinates are shifted left 4, then a single prng->Get32() is masked to a
#    byte: x takes that byte / 16 and y takes that byte % 16. So the two axes are
#    not independent, and the same draw places every ball spawned in that step.
# 5. A PICKUP IS REFUSED five ways and each one returns: a wrong packet length, a
#    player in spectator mode, a player flagged too lagged to carry, a ball id at
#    or past the count, a ball that is not on the map, and a time that does not
#    match the ball's -- that last one is the anti-cheat, and it means a client
#    replaying an old pickup is ignored. Finally, a player already carrying a ball
#    is refused SILENTLY, with no log line at all.
# 6. PICKING UP SETS THE BALL'S TIME TO 0 and its position to the PLAYER's, not to
#    where the ball was. Firing sets the time, position and speed from the packet
#    verbatim -- the server does not sanity-check any of them.
# 7. A GOAL IS GATED ON bd->carrier BEING NON-NULL, which is reused as a
#    'this goal has not been counted yet' flag: the ball is on the map and its
#    carrier field still names whoever last fired it. The second goal packet for
#    the same ball is dropped silently because SpawnBall cleared that field.
# 8. CLEANUP AFTER A CARRIER drops the ball AT THE PLAYER'S POSITION with zero
#    speed and the current tick. Whether the carrier field is cleared depends on
#    the caller: leaving, changing ship and changing freq all pass neut = 1, but a
#    KILL passes !deathgoal -- so with Soccer:AllowGoalByDeath on, a player killed
#    on a goal tile keeps the carrier field, which is exactly what lets rule 7
#    count the goal.
# 9. Cleanup's second branch, taken only when neut is set, also clears the carrier
#    of a ball that is already on the map and was last touched by that player, so
#    the last-toucher always names someone still present.
sizes BallPacket=16 C2SPickupBall=6 C2SShootBall_is_BallPacket=16 C2SGoal=6
uniforms 8 0.5 0 0.25 0.5 0.75 0.25 1 0.875
# one spawn point: every ball uses index 0
settings ballcount=2 get32=0000005a t0=1000 sendtime=1000 goaldelay=0 deathgoal=0 spawn0=512,512,10 spawn1=0,0,0 spawn2=0,0,0 spawn3=0,0,0
balls 2 0:onmap/8277/8202/0/0/-1/1000 1:onmap/8165/8202/0/0/-1/1000
pkt 2e0055200a2000000000ffffe8030000
pkt 2e01e51f0a2000000000ffffe8030000
uniforms 8 0.5 0 0.25 0.5 0.75 0.25 1 0.875
# two spawn points configured: the index is bid %% 2
settings ballcount=4 get32=0000003c t0=2000 sendtime=1000 goaldelay=0 deathgoal=0 spawn0=512,512,10 spawn1=100,900,5 spawn2=0,0,0 spawn3=0,0,0
balls 4 0:onmap/8275/8204/0/0/-1/2000 1:onmap/1587/14412/0/0/-1/2000 2:onmap/8195/8316/0/0/-1/2000 3:onmap/1651/14364/0/0/-1/2000

settings ballcount=4 get32=000000f0 t0=3000 sendtime=1000 goaldelay=0 deathgoal=0 spawn0=512,512,10 spawn1=100,900,5 spawn2=200,800,4 spawn3=300,700,3
balls 4 0:onmap/8287/8192/0/0/-1/3000 1:onmap/1599/14400/0/0/-1/3000 2:onmap/3215/12848/0/0/-1/3000 3:onmap/4847/11168/0/0/-1/3000

pkt 2e013f06403800000000ffffb80b0000

balls 4 0:onmap/8272/8207/0/0/-1/4000 1:onmap/1584/14415/0/0/-1/4000 2:onmap/8192/8319/0/0/-1/4000 3:onmap/1648/14367/0/0/-1/4000

# a draw off the left edge wraps round to the right, it does not reflect
settings ballcount=1 get32=00000000 t0=5000 sendtime=1000 goaldelay=0 deathgoal=0 spawn0=5,5,100 spawn1=0,0,5 spawn2=0,0,4 spawn3=0,700,3
